recipes.name: Skillet Apple Brownie
ingredients_raw: 2 cups apples - peeled, cored and chopped

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place an 8- or 9-inch cast iron skillet into the oven to preheat.
Whisk together flour, white sugar, brown sugar, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves in a bowl; set aside.

Beat together eggs, vanilla extract, and melted butter in a mixing bowl. Toss apples and pecans in the flour mixture, then stir into the egg mixture until combined. Melt 1 tablespoon butter in the preheated skillet, swirling to coat the pan.

Pour the batter into the hot pan, and replace into the oven. Bake until the sides are dry and a toothpick inserted into the center of the brownie comes out clean, about 40 minutes. Cool in the skillet for 20 minutes before removing and slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Skillet Apple Brownie
raw_recipe.description: This is a warm, chewy skillet apple dessert with a brownie-like texture. Served in a cast iron pan, it’s an impressive presentation, perfect for company. Serve with ice cream.

video.description: When you want a brownie that tastes like apple pie, you’ll find your happiness here. Simply preheat your skillet while you mix together flour, sugar, brown sugar, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves. Toss apples and pecans in the flour mixture, then stir into a mixture of eggs, vanilla and melted butter. Melt a pat of butter in the cast iron pan, swirling for good measure, then pour in your apple-infused batter. Bake until beautifully golden and your kitchen smells like autumn!

review.reviewBody: This is my recipe and I made it 2 nights ago and was short an egg - so I just used 1 and I liked it even better than the original version. If you like your brownies fudgy (like we do) then 1 egg is the way to go. It makes the batter stiff so I thinned it with a little milk.

I've made this at least 10 times and just love it. Our apple tree gives us so many apples and this is such an easy way to use them up! I sometimes use a small skillet and cut the recipe in half. I do add twice as many apples and walnuts. Also bake a bit longer as family likes the crunchy crust. I partially peel the apples as most of the vitamins are in the skin!

I cut the nutmeg and cloves in half (a personal preference), but otherwise made as directed. I brought this to a group dinner and everyone raved. The texture was definitely more cake than brownie. I think I may have over beat the eggs, vanilla, and melted butter. Next time I will simply stir them till well blended, use only 1 egg (to try to get a fudgier texture), cut back nutmeg and cloves to 1/4 tsp and maybe try adding toffee bits (because why not). So simple, so delicious.

Used a 10" iron skillet, so I upped the flour scant 1/2 cup. Used 3/4 cup sugar substitute and heaping tablespoon of molasses. Added 1/4 cup sour cream & 2 tablespoons milk then realized I forgot to add melted butter... added it. Patted it into preheated skillet and topped it all off with crumb topping: 1/2 Cup flour, 1/4 cup butter, scant 1/2 cup raw sugar and 1 Tablespoon cinnamon. 
I tried it too soon and it was oily, 2 hours later and it was really brownie-like; next day it is, now, even better!
Saving this recipe!

I don't have an 8-9" skillet, I increased each of the ingredients by 50% for a 10" skillet. It baked up to about 1-1/2" thick. I used apple pie spice mix, 3 Granny Smith, peeled sliced and cored with an ancient thing-a-ma-jig that does that tedious job wonderfully fast then put the cut up diced slices in a bag with all the flour and shake, dumping it in mixing bowl with the liquids and stirred. Definitely good in hot cast iron pan method. Baked for 50 minutes turned out looking like the photo. If you cook with apples frequently then get one of those thing-a-ma-jigs. Great recipe to go in the dessert recipes list. I love all apple pie flavours. Thank you smiles goes to the recipe creator.

I made this for our office Thanksgiving Potluck. I reduced the apples by a 1/2 cup and added cranberries for the theme and baked them in a cast iron muffin pan. Absolutely fantastic is all I heard anyone say. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

This was wonderful! My daughter's calling it "That yummy apple thingy" and requesting it for the second time this week! 

I just made it gluten-free (by using brown rice flour) and omitted the cloves and nutmeg (as I can't have) and it turned out great! The full amount of cinnamon was perfect and the glassware I used worked beautifully. Thanks!

We halved the amount of sugars so 1/4 cup white & 1/4 cup brown and doubled the vanilla extract. It doesn’t look appealing but it sure does taste delicious!!! I am lazy so I didn’t peel my apples and it turned out just fine. Also didn’t have ground cloves so I substituted in pumpkin pie spice. It had the perfect consistency and flavor!

This recipe was very simple and easy. My husband and I really enjoyed this blondie. I followed the recipe almost exactly. The only thing I changed was reducing the amount of cloves. I used 1/4 tsp cloves instead of 1/2 tsp. I will make this again

My husband and I are politely called apple freaks. When we saw this recipe we knew we had to make it. Easy to make and since we take great care of our cast iron pans it wasn't a worry about the batter sticking to the pan. We will reduce the amount of clove to half of what recipe calls for. Our additions were 1 tsp of baking powder and about 1/8 tsp cardamom. Also, the ice cream we put on top was Butter Cookie Ice Cream by Hudsonville. Oh la la, it was fantastic. This will be a keeper recipe for this family.

Quick and easy, and very yummy. I only made 2 changes - reduced the amount of both brown and white sugar by maybe a quarter of the recipe amount, and used homemade (white) lavender sugar I had received as a gift. It was plenty sweet even reduced. I don't have a cast iron skillet, like many of the reviewers, so used a 9x9 dish. Worked perfectly.
Good to try. A lot of spices.
I'm definitely keeping this recipe and making it again. Soooo good!!!! I didn't have ground clove so I used pumpkin pie spice like others did and it tasted great!
TY for the shattering tip. Very important, I don't have a cast iron pan yet
I have made this 3 times in the span of one month for my husband HE LOVES IT so do I. And he is kind of a picky eater, but this is a big hit for him.

Turned out great for me...I increased the ingredients by 25% because I used a 10.25" Cast Iron Skillet and came out perfect with bake time right on the 40 minutes. I used half Granny & half Honey Crisp apples. I loved all the different textures in the chew...from the caramelized crust, soft apples, and the slight crunch of the Pecans. Next time I may do Apple Pie Spice because i thought the Clove was a little too much

Turned out great! I used a 12 cast iron pan. Followed recipe except for didn’t have brown sugar or vanilla. Use regular sugar and maple syrup instead. For spices only had cinnamon. Low on butter so used avocado oil for cast iron pan.
I made this a couple days ago and used my brownie pan that makes individual brownies and it turned out amazing. Everyone loved them and they were gone in no time, I had none to bring home!
One of the best recipes I ever made from all recipes. Only had a 12" cast iron skillet so I doubled the recipe and it came out great, glad I did, whole family loved it then all asked for recipe.

I made this for our neighborhood gator, grouper and redfish cookout. I was a bit skeptical about taking something to an outing that I have never made before. However, it did not disappoint,. I got soooo many OMG’s and I need the recipe requests. Given the size of my cast iron skillet I made 1 1/2 the amount of requested ingredients and only used the 2 eggs. This is definitely a recipe I will be making again. It’s a KEEPER!!1❤️🍎❤️🍎
